The Desert’s Heartbeat on Stage

From intimate resort evenings to grand festival stages, our Rajasthani Cultural Concerts & Festivals bring the Thar Desert’s soul to life. Led by Krishna Music School Pushkar with 17+ years professional performance experience, we blend folk classics, devotional bhajans, Sufi fusion, and Bollywood grooves into immersive productions tailored for tourism boards, cultural festivals, luxury hotels/resorts, corporate MICE events, and destination weddings. Our performances feature authentic UNESCO-heritage Kalbeliya dance, Rajasthani folk instruments (harmonium, dholak, nagada, khartal, morchang), and audience engagement that transforms passive watching into participatory celebration. Scalable ensembles from intimate 4-piece quartets (₹50K) to spectacular 20+ performer troupes (₹5L+) ensure perfect fit for any venue, audience, and budget.

Folk Heritage Set

45-60 Minutes ₹50K-1.2L

Best For: Hotel cultural evenings, tourism festivals, cultural centers, intimate gatherings, boutique resort events

Repertoire Highlights:

  • Opening: Kesariya Balam (Rajasthan’s unofficial anthem—instant audience recognition and connection)
  • Medley: Padharo Mhare Desh, Mharo Rajasthan (welcoming celebratory folk classics, warm energy)
  • Dance Integration: Ghoomar performed live with dancers if selected (graceful twirling, colorful costumes)
  • Interactive: Teach audience simple folk chorus (participation creates memorable shared experience)
  • Closing: High-energy desert medley building to crescendo (leave audience energized, uplifted)

Ensemble: 4-8 musicians (harmonium, dholak, khartal, morchang, manjira, lead + backing vocals)

Audience Experience: Warm, welcoming, educational (brief song context explanations), photo-friendly moments, accessible energy

Meet the Ensemble

Our performances feature a core team of master musicians and UNESCO-heritage dancers, expandable based on event requirements.

🎹 Core Musicians

Vini Devda – Lead Vocals & Harmonium

17+ years professional performance, family lineage in Rajasthani folk music spanning generations. Trained in Hindustani classical raga, specializes in making traditional folk accessible and engaging to global audiences without diluting authenticity.

Percussion Section

  • Dholak Specialist: Folk drum master, wedding/celebration rhythms, trained in traditional village styles
  • Tabla Artist: Classical percussion for devotional/Sufi sets, trained in Benares gharana tradition
  • Nagada Thunder Drums: Dramatic entrances/processions, royal ceremonial traditions
  • Khartal & Morchang: Folk instruments adding regional Rajasthani flavor, texture layers

Backing Vocalists

2-4 chorus singers (male/female mix) for harmonies, call-response sections, group kirtan, creating full sound for larger venues.

💃 Dance Troupe (UNESCO Heritage)

Kalbeliya (Serpent Dance)

Mesmerizing hip movements mimicking cobra, dramatic swirling black skirts embroidered with mirrors. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status—authentic practitioners from Kalbeliya community, not imitators. 2-4 dancers depending on package scale.

Ghoomar (Graceful Twirling)

Traditional Rajasthani women’s dance, colorful flowing skirts creating mesmerizing circular patterns. Elegant, photogenic, audience-favorite for weddings and cultural evenings. Represents Rajput royal court traditions.

Sapera (Snake Charmer Dance)

Dramatic high-energy performance with fire pots balanced on head (optional—venue permitting). Spectacular finale element, creates gasps and photo frenzy, unforgettable visual climax to performances.

Technical Requirements: Event Planner Guide

Comprehensive technical specifications to ensure smooth production—we guide you through every detail.

🎪 Stage Requirements

Size: 20×16 ft recommended (flexible—we’ve adapted to 12×12 ft intimate venues and 40×30 ft festival stages)

Surface: Flat, stable (wooden stage ideal, concrete acceptable, avoid uneven lawns for dancer safety—ankle injuries risk)

Cover: Roofed stage preferred (protection from sun/rain), open-air acceptable with rain backup plan coordinated

Height: Minimum 2 ft elevation for audience sightlines (4-5 ft ideal for large audiences 500+)

🔊 Sound Requirements

Mixer: 16-channel minimum (32-channel ideal for larger ensembles with multiple mics/instruments)

Microphones:

  • 4-6 vocal mics (Shure SM58 or equivalent dynamic mics)
  • 2 instrument mics (for dholak, tabla if close-miking preferred)
  • 2 DI boxes (harmonium direct input, tanpura if electric tanpura used)

Monitors: 2-4 stage monitors (musicians need to hear themselves, dancers need clear music for timing)

Main Speakers: Appropriate for venue size and guest count (we advise based on specifics—indoor/outdoor matters)

We Provide: Small PA for intimate venues (<100 people). Larger events require venue/organizer sound system meeting specs.

💡 Lighting Requirements

Basic: Warm white wash covering full stage (minimum acceptable for small venues)

Enhanced: Spot lights for dance solos, colored washes for mood shifts between songs (recommended for galas)

Optional Premium: Moving heads for festival-scale productions, haze machine for atmospheric effect (dramatic but not essential)

We Provide: No lighting equipment (rely on venue/organizer), but provide lighting cue sheet upon request for tech directors

⚡ Power & Logistics

Electrical: Stable 220V AC, 15-20 amp dedicated circuit (avoid shared power with kitchen/AC—causes issues)

Backup: Generator backup essential for outdoor events (we’ve had grid failures mid-performance—backup saved shows!)

Green Room: Private changing area for performers, especially dancers (costume changes, makeup touch-ups)

Arrival Time: 2-3 hours before performance for setup, soundcheck, final coordination with event team

Parking: Vehicle access for instrument unloading (harmoniums, nagada drums heavy—need proximity)

Refreshments: Water essential, meals appreciated for multi-hour events (performer care = better performance)

Booking Process: From Inquiry to Performance

1

Initial Inquiry

Contact Via: WhatsApp +91 99286 58520 or Email krishnamusicschoolpushkar@gmail.com

Share Details:

  • Event date, location, venue type (hotel/resort/outdoor/festival stage)
  • Expected audience size and demographics (age range, Indian/international mix)
  • Describe vision (folk heritage? fusion? dance focus? devotional? multi-act spectacular?)
  • Budget range if comfortable sharing (helps us recommend appropriate format)
2

Consultation Call

Duration: 15-30 minutes phone/video call

Discussion Points:

  • Event goals, audience demographics, desired energy level and tone
  • Venue suitability assessment (stage size, acoustics, technical capabilities)
  • Recommend appropriate format/ensemble size based on requirements
  • Answer technical questions, timeline coordination, logistics planning
3

Custom Proposal

We Send Detailed Proposal Including:

  • Recommended format, ensemble lineup, performance duration
  • Complete pricing breakdown (transparent—no hidden fees)
  • Tech rider (sound/lighting/stage requirements with specifications)
  • Sample setlist (customizable based on your feedback and preferences)
  • Timeline (arrival, setup, soundcheck, performance, breakdown)
4

Contract & Advance

Agreement: Sign performance contract (details, pricing, cancellation terms, responsibilities)

Advance Payment: 30-50% advance secures date exclusively (remaining balance before/at event)

Final Coordination: Call 1-2 weeks before event (confirm logistics, timing, any last-minute adjustments)

5

Performance Day & Closure

Execution:

  • Arrive 2-3 hours early for setup, soundcheck, coordination with venue team
  • Deliver performance per agreed format, duration, and energy specifications
  • Remaining balance collected (cash/bank transfer/online payment)
  • Post-event: Share photos/videos if captured (for your promotional use if desired)

Variables Affecting Price:

  • Ensemble Size: More performers = higher cost (each additional musician/dancer adds ₹8K-15K)
  • Duration: Longer performances proportionally higher (90 mins costs ~1.5x of 60 mins)
  • Location: Travel outside Rajasthan adds logistics (transport, accommodation, per diems)
  • Production Complexity: Custom choreography, special requests, fusion elements increase cost
  • Season: Peak wedding season (Oct-March) commands 20-30% premium due to demand
  • Notice Period: Last-minute bookings (< 2 weeks) may incur rush fees if we adjust schedules
